summary:
The usual next-greater stack, but the ring wraps, so a tile near the end may find its answer near the start.
Walk the indices twice (`0 .. 2n−1`, reading `ring[i mod n]`), pushing tiles only during the first lap. The
second lap answers the tiles still waiting. O(n).

question.md:
Tiles sit in a circle. From each tile, walk clockwise and report the first strictly bigger number; −1 if no
tile on the ring is bigger.

- **Wrap-around:** after the last tile comes tile 0.
- **Strictly bigger:** equal numbers don't count, so every copy of the maximum gets −1.
- **Up to 10⁵ tiles.**

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- The maximum value (and its copies) gets −1.
- Wrap-around: the answer for a tile near the end may come from the beginning.
- One tile: −1.

think.md:
**The monotonic stack idea.** Keep a stack of items that are still **waiting for an answer** (for example "the next
warmer day"). When a new item arrives, it answers every waiting item it beats; those are popped. Because each popped
item was beaten by the new one, the items left on the stack are always in sorted order (that's the "monotonic" part),
so the new item only needs to look at the top.

**Why it's O(n).** Every item is pushed once and popped at most once, so all the `while` loops together do at most
`n` pops, even though a single step may pop many.

**Handling the circle.** Walk the tiles **twice** (`i` from 0 to `2n − 1`, tile `i mod n`). During the first lap,
push every tile; during the second lap, only answer waiting tiles, without pushing again. Any tile's next bigger
value is at most `n − 1` steps away, so two laps reach it. For `[4, 2, 7, 3, 7, 1]`:

idea.md: From each tile, walk up to `n − 1` steps clockwise (with `mod n`) until a bigger value appears.

build: For each tile, walk around the ring.

walk.title: From every tile, walk clockwise (wrapping) for up to n − 1 tiles until a bigger number.

limits.md: Walks overlap heavily. A stack over two laps answers each tile once.

approaches.title: Stack over two laps

idea.md:
Monotonic stack of waiting tile indices over two laps. Pop and answer smaller tiles whenever a bigger value
appears; push only during the first lap.

**Why two laps suffice.** The second lap shows every tile again, so a tile waiting at the end of the first
lap sees all tiles after it around the ring.

build: Loop `i` over `2n` steps using `i mod n`.

lines.text: Answers default to −1; the stack holds tiles still waiting.
Two passes over the ring; `i % n` maps the second lap back onto the tiles.
The current number is the first bigger one for every smaller tile waiting on top.
Each tile waits once, so it's pushed only in the first lap. In the second lap, tiles only answer.
Tiles still waiting are the maximum (or tied with it): −1.

complexity.md: **Time O(n):** `2n` steps, each tile pushed and popped once. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Lap 1, tile 0 (4): answers nobody. Push it.
Lap 1, tile 1 (2): answers nobody. Push it.
Lap 1, tile 2 (7): answers tiles [1, 0]. Push it.
Lap 1, tile 3 (3): answers nobody. Push it.
Lap 1, tile 4 (7): answers tiles [3]. Push it.
Lap 1, tile 5 (1): answers nobody. Push it.
Lap 2, tile 0 (4): answers tiles [5]. (Not pushed again: every tile already waits once.)
Tiles [2, 4] are the biggest numbers on the ring: −1. Answer: [7, 7, -1, 7, -1, 4].

walk.title: Run the 'next bigger' stack over the ring twice in a row (indices 0..2n−1, using i mod n). The second lap lets tiles near the end find bigger tiles near the start.

takeaways.md:
- **Circular next greater:** iterate twice, push only in the first pass.
- Two laps are enough because the answer is within `n − 1` steps.
- **Pitfall:** pushing again in the second lap (answers would be overwritten).
